description: We’re a team passionate about AI, software development, data visualization, and solving real-world problems with technology. We have experience building full-stack applications, AI-powered systems, backend services, data-driven dashboards, and interactive web experiences. For this challenge, we’re interested in turning NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS fire data into a practical, intuitive wildfire monitoring and analysis platform.
summary:
IGNIS – Beyond the Hotspot is a satellite-based wildfire intelligence platform developed to harmonize NASA's MODIS and VIIRS fire observations into meaningful fire events.

Satellite instruments often detect overlapping thermal anomalies, creating duplicate or fragmented representations of the same fire activity. IGNIS addresses this challenge through geospatial and temporal matching, bipartite assignment, and fire-event harmonization. It processes satellite observations, identifies coincident detections, groups nearby events, and provides probabilistic classification into Forest Wildfire, Agricultural Burning, Industrial Heat, and Unknown categories.

The platform features an interactive 3D Earth built with CesiumJS, allowing users to explore fire observations, harmonized events, and historical datasets. Integrated with NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), IGNIS aims to transform individual satellite detections into more accessible and actionable fire intelligence.

By reducing duplicate observations and providing contextual information, IGNIS supports better understanding of global thermal activity and demonstrates how satellite data processing can contribute to wildfire monitoring and environmental awareness.
details:
IGNIS

IGNIS is a satellite-based wildfire intelligence platform designed to transform individual thermal anomaly observations into unified and meaningful fire events.

How it works:

The platform integrates NASA FIRMS data from MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments through a Python FastAPI backend. Its harmonization engine uses geodesic distance calculations, temporal matching (2.5-hour threshold), and bipartite assignment (1.5 km matching distance) to identify observations that may represent the same fire activity.

The processed observations are organized into harmonized events and analyzed using a probabilistic classification engine that identifies potential Forest Wildfires, Agricultural Burning, Industrial Heat, or Unknown sources. Spatial clustering functionality supports grouping geographically related events.

Key Features:

  • Interactive 3D Earth visualization using CesiumJS.
  • NASA FIRMS satellite data integration.
  • MODIS–VIIRS observation harmonization.
  • Probabilistic fire-source classification.
  • Historical fire archive exploration.
  • Live data feed integration and fire-event analytics.
  • Global geographic exploration.

Technology Stack:

Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite, CSS and CesiumJS.

Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn and Pydantic.

Data Processing: Geospatial calculations, temporal matching, bipartite assignment and spatial clustering.

Database: DuckDB and PostgreSQL (Neon migration).

Deployment: Vercel and Render.

Innovation and Impact:

IGNIS goes beyond displaying individual satellite hotspots. Its primary innovation is attempting to reconcile observations from two different satellite instruments into unified fire events, reducing fragmented and potentially duplicated representations. It also recognizes that thermal anomalies do not automatically indicate wildfires, using probabilistic source classification rather than treating every detection as a confirmed forest fire.

The project aims to make satellite fire observations easier to explore, interpret and analyze, supporting environmental monitoring and better-informed fire intelligence.
